posts.cooked: Can Twisted Miscreation be killed through hit point damage while Infinitor is on Tormented Malefactor side?  Twisted Miscreation reduces all damage dealt to him to 1 and Tormented Malefactor provides a general "Damage Taken Minus 1" buff to all villain targets.  So, unless there is a timing thing involved here, damage is reduced to 1 and then 1 is subtracted from damage bringing the total to 0...unless that is reversed.  Is that reversed?

posts.name: eugeneruss
posts.cooked:
I assume we at least agree we have to apply every damage dealt modifier to the incoming damage before he can take the damage and thus reduce it, so no cheating by applying Galvanize last?

For me, I'm seeing this as related to the way you remove modifiers when they no longer apply (such as when targets change or damage types get modified), granted that process can get pretty hinky. You made the target take more damage? Great, it removes more of it now. Essentially I plan to play the card as though there's no way other than irreducible damage to cause more than a point of damage at a time, as that's the way the card reads and that's how I prefer to let it play. Knyfe's still good against it with flawless execution, as are the various destroy targets effects.

posts.name: eugeneruss
posts.cooked:
It's an interesting one, because it's a sliding scale and the others are fixed. I know the app lets you mix the order of dealt and reduced right now, and I'm not personally enamored of a situation where Fanatic fighting with Legacy hits the miscreation for four instead of two because she applies Galvanize after setting the damage to one. Wonder if it'll lead to a change, I think it leaves the card a bit impotent vs. modifiers but that may just be how the cards flop.

For the record, I'm also not enamored of applying Wraith's -1 to damage dealt after reducing damage taken with one of the 5 point reduction effects :) I'm pretty sure the app allows that one. My strong preference is that damage dealt modifiers all get applied before considering effects that alter damage taken. YMMV and >G's mileage definitely varies.

posts.name: phantaskippy
posts.cooked:
The word heal is not a game mechanic in Sentinels.

 

There is recovery, which is the only thing that gets increases and decreases.

There is regaining, which is the in game turn for the act of raising HP.  Regaining is Recovery.

Then there is restoring, which is to a certain amount, regardless of the amount before restoring.  Restoring is now clarified to not be Recovery.

 

Thanks for doing that Pydro, I had completely forgotten about that.
